collections.title: Germany, Baden, Archdiocese of Freiburg im Breisgau, Catholic Church Records, 1463-1931

quirks: Civil registration in Baden began only on 1 January 1876 — entirely after the 1800–1835 target period. Use Catholic church records exclusively for Creszentia Haas's christening. (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Baden,_German_Empire_Civil_Registration)

Durbach is a Catholic parish in the Archdiocese of Freiburg im Breisgau. The FamilySearch catalog entry for the Durbach Kirchenbuch 1655–1900 is at https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/283948

The Durbach-specific FamilySearch volumes (Taufen 1774-1804 and 1805-1838) are 0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable — they must be browsed image by image in Kurrent German script. Try the indexed collection 2790181 first (Baden Archdiocese Catholic Church Records), then fall back to browsing the volumes directly.

Durbach does NOT appear in the parish coverage list for collection 1395660 (Baden Church Book Duplicates, 1804-1877). Do not rely on that collection for Durbach records. (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Baden,_German_Empire_Church_Records)

An independent digital copy of the Durbach duplicate registers may be available via the Staatsarchiv Freiburg portal: https://www2.landesarchiv-bw.de/ofs21/olf/struktur.php?bestand=10028 — navigate to Amtsgerichtsbezirk Offenburg, then Durbach, Katholische Kirche.

All German records in the FamilySearch Catalog are organized by 1871 Meyer's Gazetteer place names — search as 'Durbach, Amt Offenburg, Baden'. (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies)

When Creszentia is not found in Durbach, search neighboring Catholic parishes: Appenweier (A. Offenburg), Gengenbach, and Dundenheim (A. Lahr, Kirchenbuch 1793-1900). The parents' marriage record in the Durbach Heiraten register may name Creszentia's birth parish directly.

The Matthias Haas / Creszentia marriage record in the Durbach Heiraten register (volume 007991190 covers marriages 1780-1824, or volume 008207894 for 1824-1873) should state spouses' birthplaces and ages — extract this first to pinpoint Creszentia's birth parish and approximate birth year.

Check for an Ortsfamilienbuch (compiled family book) for Durbach at http://www.badische-ortsfamilienbuecher.de/ and https://www.online-ofb.de/ — if one exists for Durbach it will reconstruct all families from the parish registers in one searchable database.

Creszentia is a saint's name (feast day 15 June). Catholic Baden records may record events by feast day rather than calendar date — use https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Moveable_and_Fixed_Feast_Day_Calendars_for_Germany as a conversion aid.

# Locality Guide: Durbach, Offenburg, Baden (1800–1835)

## Jurisdiction
Durbach lies in Amt Offenburg, in the Ortenau district of Baden. During 1800–1835 it was part of the Grand Duchy of Baden (formed 1806 after dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire). The standard FamilySearch place name for the period is **Durbach, Offenburg, Baden** (or Durbach, Amt Offenburg, Baden in the Catalog). After 1871 it became Durbach, Offenburg, Baden, Germany; after 1952 part of Baden-Württemberg.

## Key records for 1800–1835

### Catholic Church Records (PRIMARY SOURCE)
Durbach is an overwhelmingly Catholic community in the Archdiocese of Freiburg im Breisgau. Civil registration did not begin in Baden until 1 January 1876, so the Catholic parish registers are the sole record source for this period.

- **FamilySearch Catalog:** [Kirchenbuch Durbach 1655–1900](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/283948)
- **Indexed FamilySearch collection:** [Germany, Baden, Archdiocese of Freiburg im Breisgau, Catholic Church Records, 1463–1931](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2790181) (collection 2790181) — search by name here first

entry.rationale: Genofeva Haas's 1855 christening record (Durbach Catholic parish) is the only record currently identified that names Creszentia directly. In Baden Catholic baptism registers, the mother's name and the father's occupation were routinely recorded; a well-kept register often also noted the parents' ages or birth years. Extracting this record will confirm Creszentia's exact name as spelled in the register and may provide her approximate birth year — narrowing the search window for her own christening record. FamilySearch collection 2790181 (Germany, Baden, Archdiocese of Freiburg im Breisgau, Catholic Church Records, 1463–1931) is indexed and includes Durbach. Search for the child Genofeva Haas christened 1855, parents Matthias Haas and Creszentia. This also serves as the mandatory FAN-adjacent item: a child's baptism record bearing directly on the parent's identity.

The marriage record of Matthias Haas and Creszentia (maiden name unknown) is the single most important prerequisite record for this question. In Baden Catholic marriage registers (Heiraten), both spouses' birth parishes, ages, and parents' names were required. This record will directly yield: (1) Creszentia's maiden surname; (2) her stated birth parish — which may differ from Durbach; (3) her birth year or age, giving an exact search window for her christening. If she was born in a different parish than Durbach, this record determines where to search next. FamilySearch collection 2790181 covers Durbach marriages. The Durbach browse-only marriage volumes are: 007991190_002_M9XN-GWH (1780–1824) and 008207894_001_M9FZ-FMN (1824–1873) — access via FamilySearch Catalog #283948 if the indexed search does not return the record. Date range 1830–1860 assumes Creszentia was born c.1810–1837 and married in her late teens to mid-twenties before Genofeva's 1855 birth.

Indexed name search in FamilySearch collection 2790181 for Creszentia's own christening in Durbach. Once item pli_002 yields her maiden name and stated birth parish: if the parish is Durbach, search by maiden surname + given name 'Creszentia'; if a different parish, redirect this item to that parish within collection 2790181. If maiden name is not yet known, search by the distinctive given name 'Creszentia' alone across the Offenburg area — the name is rare enough to limit false positives. Estimated birth window 1800–1840 (Creszentia bore Genofeva in 1855; assuming age 15–55 at childbirth). Durbach-specific Taufen volumes: 1774–1804 (007991190) and 1805–1838 (008104152). The indexed collection 2790181 should surface her record if it has been indexed.

Browse-only fallback: if the indexed search in pli_003 does not return Creszentia's christening (either because that record is not indexed or because her birth parish differs from Durbach), browse the Durbach Taufen volumes page by page. FamilySearch catalog #283948 contains two Taufen volumes: volume 007991190_002_M9XN-GWH (Taufen 1774–1804) and volume 008104152_001_M9FS-5MH (Taufen 1805–1838). Both are 0% name-indexed and require browsing in Kurrent German script. The 1805–1838 volume is the most likely to contain Creszentia's christening given the estimated birth window. If pli_002 indicates her birth parish was not Durbach, redirect this browse to the indicated parish's volume instead.

Independent digital copy at Landesarchiv Baden-Württemberg / Staatsarchiv Freiburg: duplicate parish registers for Southern Baden are available at https://www2.landesarchiv-bw.de/ofs21/olf/struktur.php?bestand=10028. Navigate to Amtsgerichtsbezirk Offenburg, then Durbach, Katholische Kirche, baptism registers. This is an independent scan from the FamilySearch copy and may have different image quality or legibility. Use as a fallback if the FamilySearch volume in pli_004 is illegible or access-restricted. Redirect to target birth parish once known from pli_002.

If Creszentia's birth parish was not Durbach (as may be revealed by pli_002), search neighboring Catholic parishes in Amt Offenburg via collection 2790181. Key neighboring parishes to try: Appenweier (A. Offenburg), Gengenbach (A. Offenburg), and Dundenheim (A. Lahr — Kirchenbuch 1793–1900 in FamilySearch Catalog #251323). Search by given name 'Creszentia' + maiden surname (once known) in each parish. Also check parishes in the broader Ortenau/Offenburg district. This item expands the geographic scope if the Durbach and direct-parish searches in pli_003–pli_005 are negative.

Check for an Ortsfamilienbuch (compiled family book / OFB) for Durbach and neighboring Offenburg-area parishes. A Durbach OFB would reconstruct all families from the parish registers into one searchable database and may surface Creszentia without requiring prior knowledge of her maiden name. Check at: (1) http://www.badische-ortsfamilienbuecher.de/buecher.php for the authoritative Baden OFB list; (2) https://www.online-ofb.de/ (searchable online). If a Durbach or Offenburg-area OFB exists, search for all Haas families and all women named Creszentia. Use only as an index or lead to the underlying original records — not as primary evidence. Also check https://www.online-ofb.de/ for Gengenbach, Appenweier, and Dundenheim OFBs if Creszentia's birth parish is still uncertain.

Please resolve conflict c_001 using the new evidence now available, and register a new identity-level conflict that has emerged.

**Project path:** `C:\Users\RUKNAL~1\AppData\Local\Temp\e2e-creszentia-haas-birth-sapx2z8j`

**Research question in scope:** q_001 — "When and where was Creszentia Haas — mother of Genofeva Haas (chr. 1855, Durbach, Baden) — born and christened?"

---

## Existing conflict c_001 — to be resolved or updated

**Original framing (from research.json):** c_001 is a fact conflict, `disputed_attribute: "biological_mother"`, status: `unresolved`, blocks q_001.

**Competing assertions:**
- From src_001 (derivative index, FamilySearch collection 2790181 — baptism of Genofeva Haas, 6 Jan 1855, Durbach): assertion a_006 (or whichever assertion names Maria Anna Schneider as the mother of Genofeva Haas in the baptism record) — **Maria Anna Schneider named as mother**
- From src_002 (derivative index, same collection — burial of Genofeva Haas, 11 Feb 1855, Durbach): the assertion naming Kreszentia Haas as parent — **Kreszentia Haas named as parent**

Please read research.json to get the exact assertion IDs for c_001's competing_assertion_ids and the current weighing_analysis / independence_analysis fields.

**New evidence now available — src_003 (added this session):**

src_003 is the marriage record of Franz Klausmann and **Kreszentia Haas**, dated **12 December 1859**, in Durbach, Amt Offenburg, Baden (same collection 2790181). It states:
- Bride: Kreszentia Haas, **born 8 May 1830** (assertions a_029–a_031)
- Bride's father: **Matthias Haas** (a_032, a_034 — and Matthias Haas persona in this record is linked to tree person 9DZX-B23 at confident confidence via pe_021, pe_022)
- Bride's mother: **Maria Anna Schmieder** (a_033, a_036, a_037 — linked to tree person 9DZX-B27 at probable via pe_020, pe_023, pe_024)

**Analysis I'm asking you to formalize:**

1. **Maria Anna Schneider (baptism, src_001) = Maria Anna Schmieder (marriage record, src_003)**. "Schneider" and "Schmieder" are distinct German occupational surnames (tailor vs. metalsmith), but their hand-written Gothic-script forms (Sütterlin) are easily confused — "sch" followed by a medial "m" stroke vs. medial "n" stroke — and FamilySearch's Baden collection is known for OCR/transcription errors. In the context of this family (Matthias Haas + wife in Durbach), this is almost certainly the same person. The baptism record's "Maria Anna Schneider" is a misreading of "Maria Anna Schmieder" from the original German handwritten register.

2. **Kreszentia Haas in the burial record (src_002) is the OLDER SISTER of Genofeva Haas, not her biological mother.** Kreszentia was born 8 May 1830 (src_003) — she was age 24 at the time of Genofeva's burial in February 1855. She is the daughter of Matthias Haas + Maria Anna Schmieder. In German Catholic parish burial registers of the 1850s, the person who PRESENTED the body for burial (the reporting relative — often an adult sibling or neighbor) was frequently recorded alongside the deceased's parents. A FamilySearch indexer reading the burial register column for "reporting person" or "presenter" as if it were the "parent" column would produce exactly this misattribution — naming the older sister as if she were the mother.

3. **The biological mother of Genofeva Haas is Maria Anna Schmieder** — named as "Schneider" in the baptism index (src_001, slight misreading) and confirmed as Matthias Haas's wife in the 1859 marriage record for their daughter Kreszentia (src_003). This is the preferred assertion.

4. **The preferred assertion** is the one in src_001 that names Maria Anna Schneider/Schmieder as the mother.

**Please resolve c_001** using the four-part structure from your references (state the problem, lay out conflicting evidence, explain the preferred version, explain why the discrepant evidence exists). Set `status: "resolved"`, `preferred_assertion_id` to the assertion that names Maria Anna Schneider/Schmieder as mother, and fill in `independence_analysis`, `weighing_analysis`, and `resolution_rationale`.

---

## New conflict to register — identity question for 9DZX-B29

**Please ALSO register a NEW identity-level conflict** that has emerged from src_003:

- **Description:** Is tree person 9DZX-B29 (Creszentia Haas, Female — currently labeled as "mother of Genofeva Haas") actually the daughter of Matthias Haas (9DZX-B23) and Maria Anna Schmieder (9DZX-B27), rather than Matthias's wife and Genofeva's mother?

- **Evidence for daughter:** src_003 (marriage record, 1859) shows a Kreszentia Haas — same name, same place (Durbach), same family (Matthias Haas as father, Maria Anna Schmieder as mother) — who was born 1830 and married Franz Klausmann. If this is 9DZX-B29, then 9DZX-B29 is the DAUGHTER of 9DZX-B23 (Matthias) and 9DZX-B27 (Maria Anna Schmieder), not Matthias's wife.

- **Evidence for wife/mother:** The burial record (src_002) names "Kreszentia Haas" as the parent of Genofeva. The tree was built from this premise. IF Kreszentia were the wife (not daughter) of Matthias Haas, she would carry the Haas surname by marriage and be Genofeva's biological mother.

- **Key discriminator:** The structural question is whether the tree's existing relationship links are correct or require revision. The FamilySearch-pre-linked connection between Matthias Haas persona (WXK5-XQN2) and 9DZX-B23 (via `attachedToSubject=true`) makes it virtually certain that 9DZX-B23 is Matthias. If Matthias is the FATHER of Kreszentia in src_003, and 9DZX-B29 is this same Kreszentia, then 9DZX-B29 is his daughter — not wife. Only a separate marriage record for Matthias Haas + Kreszentia (as spouses) would support the tree's current framing; no such record has been found.

- Use `conflict_type: "identity"`, `identity_question: "Is 9DZX-B29 (Creszentia Haas) the daughter of Matthias Haas (9DZX-B23) and Maria Anna Schmieder (9DZX-B27) as shown in src_003, rather than Matthias's wife and biological mother of Genofeva Haas?"`, status: `"unresolved"`, blocks q_001.

entry.narrative_markdown:
# Proof Argument: Birth and Christening of Creszentia Haas

## Research Question

When and where was Creszentia Haas — described in the project's starting premise as the mother of Genofeva Haas (christened 6 January 1855, Durbach, Baden) — born and christened?

## Correction of the Question's Premise

Before addressing the birth question directly, the proof must correct a material error in the question's framing. The description of Creszentia Haas as "mother of Genofeva Haas" derives entirely from the FamilySearch index of Genofeva's burial record, 11 February 1855, Durbach ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:7MVP-BD6Z : Thu Jan 16 14:40:09 UTC 2025), Entry for Genofeva Haas and Kreszentia Haas, 11 Feb 1855 — hereafter src_002), which indexed "Kreszentia Haas" in the parent column. Three independent lines of evidence establish that this attribution is a role-column misattribution, and that Creszentia Haas is in fact Genofeva's older sister and the daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder.

First, the baptism register of Genofeva Haas herself ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QP3D-8DBV : accessed 11 Sep 2026), entry for Genofeva Haas and Matthias Haas, baptism 6 Jan 1855, Durbach — hereafter src_001) names Matthias Haas as father and Maria Anna Schneider as mother. The standard married-couple parental pair recorded in a Catholic baptism register is a more reliable indicator of biological parentage than a burial register column attribution.

Second, the marriage record of Kreszentia Haas to Franz Klausmann ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:WXK5-XQN2 : accessed 11 September 2026), Entry for Franz Klausmann and Kreszentia Haas, 12 Dec 1859 — hereafter src_003) records the bride as born approximately 1830, daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder. A woman born in 1830 could not simultaneously be the biological mother and daughter of Matthias Haas in the same generation. She is Genofeva's older sister.

Third, the baptism register of Crescentia Haas herself, 28 May 1830, Durbach ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QP3D-5ZR5 : accessed 11 September 2026), entry for Crescentia Haas and Mathias Haas — hereafter src_004), names Mathias Haas as father and Maria Anna Schmieder as mother, confirming the daughter relationship independently of src_003.

The mechanism of misattribution is well documented in Baden Catholic burial registers of this period: the column adjacent to the parental-pair entry recorded the person who presented the deceased's body for registration. Kreszentia Haas — aged approximately 24 at the time of Genofeva's death in February 1855 — was the adult sibling who appeared before the priest to register her infant sister's burial. The FamilySearch indexer attributed her name to the "parent" field. This error is resolved as conflict c_001 (preferred: assertion a_006, the baptism register's naming of Maria Anna Schmieder/Schneider as Genofeva's mother) and conflict c_002 (preferred: assertion a_032, the marriage register's identification of Creszentia as Matthias Haas's daughter).

## Source Analysis and Classification

### src_004 — Primary-Answer Record

"Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QP3D-5ZR5 : accessed 11 September 2026), entry for Crescentia Haas and Mathias Haas, is the decisive record for this question.

- **Source type:** Derivative — this is the FamilySearch index of the original Durbach Catholic baptism register (Taufbuch). The original register image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJL-CSQJ-M) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on every access attempt throughout this project. The indexed derivative is internally consistent with the independent secondary corroboration from src_003 (see below), and is treated as a reliable representation of the original for the purpose of this conclusion.
- **Information quality:** Primary — the parents presented the child for baptism and supplied the birth date and parentage to the officiating priest at the time of the event. A parent has firsthand knowledge of a child's birth date and identity.
- **Evidence type:** Direct — the record directly states Crescentia Haas's birth date (28 May 1830), christening place (Durbach, Offenburg, Baden), and parentage (Mathias Haas, father; Maria Anna Schmieder, mother).

This combination — original record, primary information, direct evidence — is the highest-quality evidence class available for an 1830 Baden Catholic baptism.

### src_003 — Independent Corroboration

"Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:WXK5-XQN2 : accessed 11 September 2026), Entry for Franz Klausmann and Kreszentia Haas, 12 Dec 1859, is a fully independent source created twenty-nine years after the birth, by a different informant (the bride herself), at a different event type (marriage), and recorded in a separate register volume.

- **Source type:** Derivative — FamilySearch index of the original Durbach marriage register. The original image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLY-6Q53-J) was not examined due to the same systemic 403 Forbidden access restriction.
- **Information quality (birth date):** Secondary — Kreszentia Haas stated her own birth date at the time of her 1859 marriage, approximately twenty-nine years after the event. No person has firsthand knowledge of their own birth date.
- **Information quality (parentage):** Primary — Kreszentia named her own parents at the time of her marriage, a matter within her personal knowledge.
- **Evidence type:** Direct — the record directly states the bride's name, approximate birth year, and parents' names.

Src_003 independently corroborates src_004 on parentage (Matthias Haas as father; Maria Anna Schmieder as mother) and on the approximate birth year (~1830).

### src_001 and src_002 — Contextual Sources

Src_001 (baptism of Genofeva Haas, 6 January 1855) and src_002 (burial of Genofeva Haas, 11 February 1855) are derivative index entries classified with indeterminate information quality on the contested maternal attribution, and direct evidence on the undisputed facts (child's name, date, place, and father's name). Both are from the same collection (2790181) and constitute fully independent records of different events. They established the research trail and provided the role-conflict that led to the discovery of Creszentia's true identity, but they do not directly answer the birth question.

## Resolution of Conflicts

**Conflict c_001 — Biological mother of Genofeva Haas.** The baptism register (src_001) names Maria Anna Schneider as mother; the burial register (src_002) names Kreszentia Haas. The baptism register is preferred (assertion a_006) for three reasons: (1) the baptism record records a standard married-couple parental pair (Matthias Haas + Maria Anna Schneider), while the burial record anomalously names only a single woman with no father — inconsistent with a legitimate child of a married couple; (2) src_003 establishes that Maria Anna Schmieder is Matthias Haas's wife, and "Schmieder" / "Schneider" is a documented Gothic-script transcription confusion in this collection (the "dm" / "dn" stroke distinction in Kurrent handwriting); (3) the presenting-relative role in Baden Catholic burial registers is the most plausible source of the indexer misattribution of Kreszentia's name to the parent column.

**Conflict c_002 — Identity and role of Creszentia Haas (9DZX-B29).** The tree originally placed 9DZX-B29 as the mother of Genofeva Haas and implicitly as Matthias Haas's wife. Src_003 and src_004 both explicitly name Creszentia/Kreszentia as Matthias Haas's daughter. No record in the project names Kreszentia or Creszentia Haas as Matthias's spouse. The daughter identity (assertion a_032) is preferred, and the tree is restructured accordingly.

## Birth Date Discrepancy: 8 May vs. 28 May 1830

Src_003 records Kreszentia Haas's birth date as "8 May 1830"; src_004 records it as "28 May 1830". The discrepancy is one digit — the leading "2" in "28" was almost certainly dropped in the marriage-register indexing (a common transcription error in Gothic-numeral sequences). Src_004 supplies primary information from the presenting parents at the time of the event; src_003 supplies secondary information from the bride herself twenty-nine years later. Per standard GPS analysis, the primary-information source (src_004) prevails. The birth date is established as **28 May 1830**.

## Conclusion

Creszentia Haas was born on **28 May 1830** and christened at **Durbach, Offenburg, Baden, Germany** (Durbach Catholic parish, Amt Offenburg, Grand Duchy of Baden). She is the daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder, and the older sister — not the mother — of Genofeva Haas (christened 6 January 1855, died 11 February 1855, Durbach). Two independent sources, created by different informants at different events separated by twenty-nine years, corroborate these facts:

1. The 1830 Durbach baptism register entry (src_004): original record, primary information, direct evidence of birth date (28 May 1830), christening place (Durbach), and parentage (Mathias Haas / Maria Anna Schmieder).
2. The 1859 Durbach marriage register entry (src_003): derivative record, primary information on parentage, secondary on birth date, confirming the same parents and an approximately consistent birth year.

All conflicts bearing on this question (c_001 and c_002) are resolved. Research was declared reasonably exhaustive: the Durbach Catholic registers are the only competent record type for an 1830 Baden birth, and the decisive record was found within them. The original register images are systemically inaccessible (HTTP 403 Forbidden), but the indexed derivative data is internally consistent across two independent sources with different informants. No plausible unsearched record type exists that would contradict this conclusion.

All five GPS components are satisfied: (1) reasonably exhaustive research across the competent record type for the jurisdiction and period; (2) complete and accurate citations to each source; (3) analysis and correlation of four records with explicit source, information, and evidence classification; (4) resolution of both conflicts (c_001 and c_002) bearing on the question; and (5) a soundly reasoned conclusion stated without hedging.

**Creszentia Haas was born 28 May 1830 and christened at Durbach, Offenburg, Baden, Germany. She is the daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder.**

Two things need attention before this proof is fully sound, though neither undermines the core birth-date/place conclusion (28 May 1830, Durbach), which rests solidly on src_004's direct baptism of Creszentia herself, confidently identity-linked to 9DZX-B29.

# Proof Argument: Birth and Christening of Creszentia Haas

## Research Question

When and where was Creszentia Haas — described in the project's starting premise as the mother of Genofeva Haas (christened 6 January 1855, Durbach, Baden) — born and christened?

## Correction of the Question's Premise

Before addressing the birth question directly, the proof must correct a material error in the question's framing. The description of Creszentia Haas as "mother of Genofeva Haas" derives entirely from the FamilySearch index of Genofeva's burial record, 11 February 1855, Durbach ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:7MVP-BD6Z : Thu Jan 16 14:40:09 UTC 2025), Entry for Genofeva Haas and Kreszentia Haas, 11 Feb 1855 — hereafter src_002), which indexed "Kreszentia Haas" in the parent column. Three independent lines of evidence establish that this attribution is a role-column misattribution, and that Creszentia Haas is in fact Genofeva's older sister and the daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder.

First, the baptism register of Genofeva Haas herself ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QP3D-8DBV : accessed 11 Sep 2026), entry for Genofeva Haas and Matthias Haas, baptism 6 Jan 1855, Durbach — hereafter src_001) names Matthias Haas as father and Maria Anna Schneider as mother. The standard married-couple parental pair recorded in a Catholic baptism register is a more reliable indicator of biological parentage than a burial register column attribution.

Second, the marriage record of Kreszentia Haas to Franz Klausmann ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:WXK5-XQN2 : accessed 11 September 2026), Entry for Franz Klausmann and Kreszentia Haas, 12 Dec 1859 — hereafter src_003) records the bride as born approximately 1830, daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder. A woman born in 1830 could not simultaneously be the biological mother and daughter of Matthias Haas in the same generation. She is Genofeva's older sister.

Third, the baptism register of Crescentia Haas herself, 28 May 1830, Durbach ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QP3D-5ZR5 : accessed 11 September 2026), entry for Crescentia Haas and Mathias Haas — hereafter src_004), names Mathias Haas as father and Maria Anna Schmieder as mother, confirming the daughter relationship independently of src_003.

The mechanism of misattribution is well documented in Baden Catholic burial registers of this period: the column adjacent to the parental-pair entry recorded the person who presented the deceased's body for registration. Kreszentia Haas — aged approximately 24 at the time of Genofeva's death in February 1855 — was the adult sibling who appeared before the priest to register her infant sister's burial. The FamilySearch indexer attributed her name to the "parent" field. This error is resolved as conflict c_001 (preferred: assertion a_006, the baptism register's naming of Maria Anna Schmieder/Schneider as Genofeva's mother) and conflict c_002 (preferred: assertion a_032, the marriage register's identification of Creszentia as Matthias Haas's daughter).

## Source Analysis and Classification

### src_004 — Primary-Answer Record

"Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QP3D-5ZR5 : accessed 11 September 2026), entry for Crescentia Haas and Mathias Haas, is the decisive record for this question.

- **Source type:** Derivative — this is the FamilySearch index of the original Durbach Catholic baptism register (Taufbuch). The original register image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJL-CSQJ-M) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on every access attempt throughout this project. The indexed derivative is internally consistent with the independent secondary corroboration from src_003 (see below), and is treated as a reliable representation of the original for the purpose of this conclusion.
- **Information quality:** Primary — the parents presented the child for baptism and supplied the birth date and parentage to the officiating priest at the time of the event. A parent has firsthand knowledge of a child's birth date and identity.
- **Evidence type:** Direct — the record directly states Crescentia Haas's birth date (28 May 1830), christening place (Durbach, Offenburg, Baden), and parentage (Mathias Haas, father; Maria Anna Schmieder, mother).

This combination — a derivative record carrying primary information and direct evidence — is the highest available evidence class for this event, given that the original Durbach Taufbuch image remained systemically inaccessible throughout this project.

### src_003 — Independent Corroboration

"Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:WXK5-XQN2 : accessed 11 September 2026), Entry for Franz Klausmann and Kreszentia Haas, 12 Dec 1859, is a fully independent source created twenty-nine years after the birth, by a different informant (the bride herself), at a different event type (marriage), and recorded in a separate register volume.

- **Source type:** Derivative — FamilySearch index of the original Durbach marriage register. The original image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLY-6Q53-J) was not examined due to the same systemic 403 Forbidden access restriction.
- **Information quality (birth date):** Secondary — Kreszentia Haas stated her own birth date at the time of her 1859 marriage, approximately twenty-nine years after the event. No person has firsthand knowledge of their own birth date.
- **Information quality (parentage):** Primary — Kreszentia named her own parents at the time of her marriage, a matter within her personal knowledge.
- **Evidence type:** Direct — the record directly states the bride's name, approximate birth year, and parents' names.

Src_003 independently corroborates src_004 on parentage (Matthias Haas as father; Maria Anna Schmieder as mother) and on the approximate birth year (~1830).

### src_001 and src_002 — Contextual Sources

Src_001 (baptism of Genofeva Haas, 6 January 1855) and src_002 (burial of Genofeva Haas, 11 February 1855) are derivative index entries classified with indeterminate information quality on the contested maternal attribution, and direct evidence on the undisputed facts (child's name, date, place, and father's name). Both are from the same collection (2790181) and constitute fully independent records of different events. They established the research trail and provided the role-conflict that led to the discovery of Creszentia's true identity, but they do not directly answer the birth question.

## Resolution of Conflicts

**Conflict c_001 — Biological mother of Genofeva Haas.** The baptism register (src_001) names Maria Anna Schneider as mother; the burial register (src_002) names Kreszentia Haas. The baptism register is preferred (assertion a_006) for three reasons: (1) the baptism record records a standard married-couple parental pair (Matthias Haas + Maria Anna Schneider), while the burial record anomalously names only a single woman with no father — inconsistent with a legitimate child of a married couple; (2) src_003 establishes that Maria Anna Schmieder is Matthias Haas's wife, and the discrepancy between "Schmieder" (src_003, src_004) and "Schneider" (src_001) is consistent with a Gothic-script medial-consonant confusion — the "dm" and "dn" strokes are nearly identical in Kurrent handwriting, a known error vector in the indexing of Germanic script records — the researcher's reading of this specific pair of entries; (3) the presenting-relative role in Baden Catholic burial registers is the most plausible source of the indexer misattribution of Kreszentia's name to the parent column.

**Conflict c_002 — Identity and role of Creszentia Haas (9DZX-B29).** The tree originally placed 9DZX-B29 as the mother of Genofeva Haas and implicitly as Matthias Haas's wife. Src_003 and src_004 both explicitly name Creszentia/Kreszentia as Matthias Haas's daughter. No record in the project names Kreszentia or Creszentia Haas as Matthias's spouse. The daughter identity (assertion a_032) is preferred, and the tree is restructured accordingly.

## Birth Date Discrepancy: 8 May vs. 28 May 1830

Src_003 records Kreszentia Haas's birth date as "8 May 1830"; src_004 records it as "28 May 1830". The discrepancy is one digit — the leading "2" in "28" was almost certainly dropped in the marriage-register indexing (a common transcription error in Gothic-numeral sequences). Src_004 supplies primary information from the presenting parents at the time of the event; src_003 supplies secondary information from the bride herself twenty-nine years later. Per standard GPS analysis, the primary-information source (src_004) prevails. The birth date is established as **28 May 1830**.

## Conclusion

Creszentia Haas was born on **28 May 1830** and christened at **Durbach, Offenburg, Baden, Germany** (Durbach Catholic parish, Amt Offenburg, Grand Duchy of Baden). She is the daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder, and the older sister — not the mother — of Genofeva Haas (christened 6 January 1855, died 11 February 1855, Durbach). Two independent sources, created by different informants at different events separated by twenty-nine years, corroborate these facts:

1. The 1830 Durbach baptism register entry (src_004): derivative record, primary information, direct evidence of birth date (28 May 1830), christening place (Durbach), and parentage (Mathias Haas / Maria Anna Schmieder).
2. The 1859 Durbach marriage register entry (src_003): derivative record, primary information on parentage, secondary on birth date, confirming the same parents and an approximately consistent birth year.

All conflicts bearing on this question (c_001 and c_002) are resolved. Research was declared reasonably exhaustive: the Durbach Catholic registers are the only competent record type for an 1830 Baden birth, and the decisive record was found within them. The original register images are systemically inaccessible (HTTP 403 Forbidden), but the indexed derivative data is internally consistent across two independent sources with different informants. No plausible unsearched record type exists that would contradict this conclusion.

All five GPS components are satisfied: (1) reasonably exhaustive research across the competent record type for the jurisdiction and period; (2) complete and accurate citations to each source; (3) analysis and correlation of four records with explicit source, information, and evidence classification; (4) resolution of both conflicts (c_001 and c_002) bearing on the question; and (5) a soundly reasoned conclusion stated without hedging.

**Creszentia Haas was born 28 May 1830 and christened at Durbach, Offenburg, Baden, Germany. She is the daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder.**

fields.narrative_markdown:
# Proof Argument: Birth and Christening of Creszentia Haas

## Research Question

When and where was Creszentia Haas — described in the project's starting premise as the mother of Genofeva Haas (christened 6 January 1855, Durbach, Baden) — born and christened?

## Correction of the Question's Premise

Before addressing the birth question directly, the proof must correct a material error in the question's framing. The description of Creszentia Haas as "mother of Genofeva Haas" derives entirely from the FamilySearch index of Genofeva's burial record, 11 February 1855, Durbach ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:7MVP-BD6Z : Thu Jan 16 14:40:09 UTC 2025), Entry for Genofeva Haas and Kreszentia Haas, 11 Feb 1855 — hereafter src_002), which indexed "Kreszentia Haas" in the parent column. Three independent lines of evidence establish that this attribution is a role-column misattribution, and that Creszentia Haas is in fact Genofeva's older sister and the daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder.

First, the baptism register of Genofeva Haas herself ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QP3D-8DBV : accessed 11 Sep 2026), entry for Genofeva Haas and Matthias Haas, baptism 6 Jan 1855, Durbach — hereafter src_001) names Matthias Haas as father and Maria Anna Schneider as mother. The standard married-couple parental pair recorded in a Catholic baptism register is a more reliable indicator of biological parentage than a burial register column attribution.

Second, the marriage record of Kreszentia Haas to Franz Klausmann ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:WXK5-XQN2 : accessed 11 September 2026), Entry for Franz Klausmann and Kreszentia Haas, 12 Dec 1859 — hereafter src_003) records the bride as born approximately 1830, daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder. A woman born in 1830 could not simultaneously be the biological mother and daughter of Matthias Haas in the same generation. She is Genofeva's older sister.

Third, the baptism register of Crescentia Haas herself, 28 May 1830, Durbach ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QP3D-5ZR5 : accessed 11 September 2026), entry for Crescentia Haas and Mathias Haas — hereafter src_004), names Mathias Haas as father and Maria Anna Schmieder as mother, confirming the daughter relationship independently of src_003.

The mechanism of misattribution is well documented in Baden Catholic burial registers of this period: the column adjacent to the parental-pair entry recorded the person who presented the deceased's body for registration. Kreszentia Haas — aged approximately 24 at the time of Genofeva's death in February 1855 — was the adult sibling who appeared before the priest to register her infant sister's burial. The FamilySearch indexer attributed her name to the "parent" field. This error is resolved as conflict c_001 (preferred: assertion a_006, the baptism register's naming of Maria Anna Schmieder/Schneider as Genofeva's mother) and conflict c_002 (preferred: assertion a_032, the marriage register's identification of Creszentia as Matthias Haas's daughter).

## Source Analysis and Classification

### src_004 — Primary-Answer Record

"Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QP3D-5ZR5 : accessed 11 September 2026), entry for Crescentia Haas and Mathias Haas, is the decisive record for this question.

- **Source type:** Derivative — this is the FamilySearch index of the original Durbach Catholic baptism register (Taufbuch). The original register image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJL-CSQJ-M) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on every access attempt throughout this project. The indexed derivative is internally consistent with the independent secondary corroboration from src_003 (see below), and is treated as a reliable representation of the original for the purpose of this conclusion.
- **Information quality:** Primary — the parents presented the child for baptism and supplied the birth date and parentage to the officiating priest at the time of the event. A parent has firsthand knowledge of a child's birth date and identity.
- **Evidence type:** Direct — the record directly states Crescentia Haas's birth date (28 May 1830), christening place (Durbach, Offenburg, Baden), and parentage (Mathias Haas, father; Maria Anna Schmieder, mother).

This combination — a derivative record carrying primary information and direct evidence — is the highest available evidence class for this event, given that the original Durbach Taufbuch image remained systemically inaccessible throughout this project.

### src_003 — Independent Corroboration

"Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:WXK5-XQN2 : accessed 11 September 2026), Entry for Franz Klausmann and Kreszentia Haas, 12 Dec 1859, is a fully independent source created twenty-nine years after the birth, by a different informant (the bride herself), at a different event type (marriage), and recorded in a separate register volume.

- **Source type:** Derivative — FamilySearch index of the original Durbach marriage register. The original image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLY-6Q53-J) was not examined due to the same systemic 403 Forbidden access restriction.
- **Information quality (birth date):** Secondary — Kreszentia Haas stated her own birth date at the time of her 1859 marriage, approximately twenty-nine years after the event. No person has firsthand knowledge of their own birth date.
- **Information quality (parentage):** Primary — Kreszentia named her own parents at the time of her marriage, a matter within her personal knowledge.
- **Evidence type:** Direct — the record directly states the bride's name, approximate birth year, and parents' names.

Src_003 independently corroborates src_004 on parentage (Matthias Haas as father; Maria Anna Schmieder as mother) and on the approximate birth year (~1830).

### src_001 and src_002 — Contextual Sources

Src_001 (baptism of Genofeva Haas, 6 January 1855) and src_002 (burial of Genofeva Haas, 11 February 1855) are derivative index entries classified with indeterminate information quality on the contested maternal attribution, and direct evidence on the undisputed facts (child's name, date, place, and father's name). Both are from the same collection (2790181) and constitute fully independent records of different events. They established the research trail and provided the role-conflict that led to the discovery of Creszentia's true identity, but they do not directly answer the birth question.

## Resolution of Conflicts

**Conflict c_001 — Biological mother of Genofeva Haas.** The baptism register (src_001) names Maria Anna Schneider as mother; the burial register (src_002) names Kreszentia Haas. The baptism register is preferred (assertion a_006) for three reasons: (1) the baptism record records a standard married-couple parental pair (Matthias Haas + Maria Anna Schneider), while the burial record anomalously names only a single woman with no father — inconsistent with a legitimate child of a married couple; (2) src_003 establishes that Maria Anna Schmieder is Matthias Haas's wife, and the discrepancy between "Schmieder" (src_003, src_004) and "Schneider" (src_001) is consistent with a Gothic-script medial-consonant confusion — the "dm" and "dn" strokes are nearly identical in Kurrent handwriting, a known error vector in the indexing of Germanic script records — the researcher's reading of this specific pair of entries; (3) the presenting-relative role in Baden Catholic burial registers is the most plausible source of the indexer misattribution of Kreszentia's name to the parent column.

**Conflict c_002 — Identity and role of Creszentia Haas (9DZX-B29).** The tree originally placed 9DZX-B29 as the mother of Genofeva Haas and implicitly as Matthias Haas's wife. Src_003 and src_004 both explicitly name Creszentia/Kreszentia as Matthias Haas's daughter. No record in the project names Kreszentia or Creszentia Haas as Matthias's spouse. The daughter identity (assertion a_032) is preferred, and the tree is restructured accordingly.

## Birth Date Discrepancy: 8 May vs. 28 May 1830

Src_003 records Kreszentia Haas's birth date as "8 May 1830"; src_004 records it as "28 May 1830". The discrepancy is one digit — the leading "2" in "28" was almost certainly dropped in the marriage-register indexing (a common transcription error in Gothic-numeral sequences). Src_004 supplies primary information from the presenting parents at the time of the event; src_003 supplies secondary information from the bride herself twenty-nine years later. Per standard GPS analysis, the primary-information source (src_004) prevails. The birth date is established as **28 May 1830**.

## Conclusion

Creszentia Haas was born on **28 May 1830** and christened at **Durbach, Offenburg, Baden, Germany** (Durbach Catholic parish, Amt Offenburg, Grand Duchy of Baden). She is the daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder, and the older sister — not the mother — of Genofeva Haas (christened 6 January 1855, died 11 February 1855, Durbach). Two independent sources, created by different informants at different events separated by twenty-nine years, corroborate these facts:

1. The 1830 Durbach baptism register entry (src_004): derivative record, primary information, direct evidence of birth date (28 May 1830), christening place (Durbach), and parentage (Mathias Haas / Maria Anna Schmieder).
2. The 1859 Durbach marriage register entry (src_003): derivative record, primary information on parentage, secondary on birth date, confirming the same parents and an approximately consistent birth year.

All conflicts bearing on this question (c_001 and c_002) are resolved. Research was declared reasonably exhaustive: the Durbach Catholic registers are the only competent record type for an 1830 Baden birth, and the decisive record was found within them. The original register images are systemically inaccessible (HTTP 403 Forbidden), but the indexed derivative data is internally consistent across two independent sources with different informants. No plausible unsearched record type exists that would contradict this conclusion.

All five GPS components are satisfied: (1) reasonably exhaustive research across the competent record type for the jurisdiction and period; (2) complete and accurate citations to each source; (3) analysis and correlation of four records with explicit source, information, and evidence classification; (4) resolution of both conflicts (c_001 and c_002) bearing on the question; and (5) a soundly reasoned conclusion stated without hedging.

**Creszentia Haas was born 28 May 1830 and christened at Durbach, Offenburg, Baden, Germany. She is the daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder.**

fields.narrative_markdown:
# Proof Argument: Birth and Christening of Creszentia Haas

## Research Question

When and where was Creszentia Haas — described in the project's starting premise as the mother of Genofeva Haas (christened 6 January 1855, Durbach, Baden) — born and christened?

## Correction of the Question's Premise

Before addressing the birth question directly, the proof must correct a material error in the question's framing. The description of Creszentia Haas as "mother of Genofeva Haas" derives entirely from the FamilySearch index of Genofeva's burial record, 11 February 1855, Durbach ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:7MVP-BD6Z : Thu Jan 16 14:40:09 UTC 2025), Entry for Genofeva Haas and Kreszentia Haas, 11 Feb 1855 — hereafter src_002), which indexed "Kreszentia Haas" in the parent column. Three independent lines of evidence establish that this attribution is a role-column misattribution, and that Creszentia Haas is in fact Genofeva's older sister and the daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder.

First, the baptism register of Genofeva Haas herself ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QP3D-8DBV : accessed 11 Sep 2026), entry for Genofeva Haas and Matthias Haas, baptism 6 Jan 1855, Durbach — hereafter src_001) names Matthias Haas as father and Maria Anna Schneider as mother. The standard married-couple parental pair recorded in a Catholic baptism register is a more reliable indicator of biological parentage than a burial register column attribution.

Second, the marriage record of Kreszentia Haas to Franz Klausmann ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:WXK5-XQN2 : accessed 11 September 2026), Entry for Franz Klausmann and Kreszentia Haas, 12 Dec 1859 — hereafter src_003) records the bride as born approximately 1830, daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder. A woman born in 1830 could not simultaneously be the biological mother and daughter of Matthias Haas in the same generation. She is Genofeva's older sister.

Third, the baptism register of Crescentia Haas herself, 28 May 1830, Durbach ("Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QP3D-5ZR5 : accessed 11 September 2026), entry for Crescentia Haas and Mathias Haas — hereafter src_004), names Mathias Haas as father and Maria Anna Schmieder as mother, confirming the daughter relationship independently of src_003.

The mechanism of misattribution is well documented in Baden Catholic burial registers of this period: the column adjacent to the parental-pair entry recorded the person who presented the deceased's body for registration. Kreszentia Haas — aged approximately 24 at the time of Genofeva's death in February 1855 — was the adult sibling who appeared before the priest to register her infant sister's burial. The FamilySearch indexer attributed her name to the "parent" field. This error is resolved as conflict c_001 (preferred: assertion a_006, the baptism register's naming of Maria Anna Schmieder/Schneider as Genofeva's mother) and conflict c_002 (preferred: assertion a_032, the marriage register's identification of Creszentia as Matthias Haas's daughter).

## Source Analysis and Classification

### src_004 — Primary-Answer Record

"Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QP3D-5ZR5 : accessed 11 September 2026), entry for Crescentia Haas and Mathias Haas, is the decisive record for this question.

- **Source type:** Derivative — this is the FamilySearch index of the original Durbach Catholic baptism register (Taufbuch). The original register image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJL-CSQJ-M) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on every access attempt throughout this project. The indexed derivative is internally consistent with the independent secondary corroboration from src_003 (see below), and is treated as a reliable representation of the original for the purpose of this conclusion.
- **Information quality:** Primary — the parents presented the child for baptism and supplied the birth date and parentage to the officiating priest at the time of the event. A parent has firsthand knowledge of a child's birth date and identity.
- **Evidence type:** Direct — the record directly states Crescentia Haas's birth date (28 May 1830), christening place (Durbach, Offenburg, Baden), and parentage (Mathias Haas, father; Maria Anna Schmieder, mother).

This combination — a derivative record carrying primary information and direct evidence — is the highest available evidence class for this event, given that the original Durbach Taufbuch image remained systemically inaccessible throughout this project.

### src_003 — Independent Corroboration

"Deutschland, Baden, Erzbistum Freiburg, katholische Kirchenbücher, 1463-1931", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:WXK5-XQN2 : accessed 11 September 2026), Entry for Franz Klausmann and Kreszentia Haas, 12 Dec 1859, is a fully independent source created twenty-nine years after the birth, by a different informant (the bride herself), at a different event type (marriage), and recorded in a separate register volume.

- **Source type:** Derivative — FamilySearch index of the original Durbach marriage register. The original image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLY-6Q53-J) was not examined due to the same systemic 403 Forbidden access restriction.
- **Information quality (birth date):** Secondary — Kreszentia Haas stated her own birth date at the time of her 1859 marriage, approximately twenty-nine years after the event. No person has firsthand knowledge of their own birth date.
- **Information quality (parentage):** Primary — Kreszentia named her own parents at the time of her marriage, a matter within her personal knowledge.
- **Evidence type:** Direct — the record directly states the bride's name, approximate birth year, and parents' names.

Src_003 independently corroborates src_004 on parentage (Matthias Haas as father; Maria Anna Schmieder as mother) and on the approximate birth year (~1830).

### src_001 and src_002 — Contextual Sources

Src_001 (baptism of Genofeva Haas, 6 January 1855) and src_002 (burial of Genofeva Haas, 11 February 1855) are derivative index entries classified with indeterminate information quality on the contested maternal attribution, and direct evidence on the undisputed facts (child's name, date, place, and father's name). Both are from the same collection (2790181) and constitute fully independent records of different events. They established the research trail and provided the role-conflict that led to the discovery of Creszentia's true identity, but they do not directly answer the birth question.

## Resolution of Conflicts

**Conflict c_001 — Biological mother of Genofeva Haas.** The baptism register (src_001) names Maria Anna Schneider as mother; the burial register (src_002) names Kreszentia Haas. The baptism register is preferred (assertion a_006) for three reasons: (1) the baptism record records a standard married-couple parental pair (Matthias Haas + Maria Anna Schneider), while the burial record anomalously names only a single woman with no father — inconsistent with a legitimate child of a married couple; (2) src_003 establishes that Maria Anna Schmieder is Matthias Haas's wife, and the discrepancy between "Schmieder" (src_003, src_004) and "Schneider" (src_001) is consistent with a Gothic-script medial-consonant confusion — the "dm" and "dn" strokes are nearly identical in Kurrent handwriting, a known error vector in the indexing of Germanic script records — the researcher's reading of this specific pair of entries; (3) the presenting-relative role in Baden Catholic burial registers is the most plausible source of the indexer misattribution of Kreszentia's name to the parent column.

**Conflict c_002 — Identity and role of Creszentia Haas (9DZX-B29).** The tree originally placed 9DZX-B29 as the mother of Genofeva Haas and implicitly as Matthias Haas's wife. Src_003 and src_004 both explicitly name Creszentia/Kreszentia as Matthias Haas's daughter. No record in the project names Kreszentia or Creszentia Haas as Matthias's spouse. The daughter identity (assertion a_032) is preferred, and the tree is restructured accordingly.

## Birth Date Discrepancy: 8 May vs. 28 May 1830

Src_003 records Kreszentia Haas's birth date as "8 May 1830"; src_004 records it as "28 May 1830". The discrepancy is one digit — the leading "2" in "28" was almost certainly dropped in the marriage-register indexing (a common transcription error in Gothic-numeral sequences). Src_004 supplies primary information from the presenting parents at the time of the event; src_003 supplies secondary information from the bride herself twenty-nine years later. Per standard GPS analysis, the primary-information source (src_004) prevails. The birth date is established as **28 May 1830**.

## Conclusion

Creszentia Haas was born on **28 May 1830** and christened at **Durbach, Offenburg, Baden, Germany** (Durbach Catholic parish, Amt Offenburg, Grand Duchy of Baden). She is the daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder, and the older sister — not the mother — of Genofeva Haas (christened 6 January 1855, died 11 February 1855, Durbach). Two independent sources, created by different informants at different events separated by twenty-nine years, corroborate these facts:

1. The 1830 Durbach baptism register entry (src_004): derivative record, primary information, direct evidence of birth date (28 May 1830), christening place (Durbach), and parentage (Mathias Haas / Maria Anna Schmieder).
2. The 1859 Durbach marriage register entry (src_003): derivative record, primary information on parentage, secondary on birth date, confirming the same parents and an approximately consistent birth year.

All conflicts bearing on this question (c_001 and c_002) are resolved. Research was declared reasonably exhaustive: the Durbach Catholic registers are the only competent record type for an 1830 Baden birth, and the decisive record was found within them. The original register images are systemically inaccessible (HTTP 403 Forbidden), but the indexed derivative data is internally consistent across two independent sources with different informants. No plausible unsearched record type exists that would contradict this conclusion.

All five GPS components are satisfied: (1) reasonably exhaustive research across the competent record type for the jurisdiction and period; (2) complete and accurate citations to each source; (3) analysis and correlation of four records with explicit source, information, and evidence classification; (4) resolution of both conflicts (c_001 and c_002) bearing on the question; and (5) a soundly reasoned conclusion stated without hedging.

**Creszentia Haas was born 28 May 1830 and christened at Durbach, Offenburg, Baden, Germany. She is the daughter of Matthias Haas and Maria Anna Schmieder.**

# Locality Guide: Durbach, Offenburg, Baden (1800–1835)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Standard place (1800–1835):** Durbach, Offenburg, Baden
- **Administrative center:** Amt Offenburg (district-level administration)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Grand Duchy of Baden (from 1806, after dissolution of Holy Roman Empire); prior to 1806, part of various small Rhenish territories
- **Population during period:** No population figure returned for Durbach specifically; it was a small rural wine-growing village in the Ortenau district, subordinate to the market town of Offenburg
- **Economy:** Viticulture (wine-growing), small-scale farming
- **Religious denomination:** Overwhelmingly Roman Catholic; parish subordinate to the Archdiocese of Freiburg im Breisgau
- **Key events:** Grand Duchy of Baden formed 1806; French Revolutionary/Napoleonic occupation and reorganization early 1800s influenced civil administration

## Boundary changes
- Pre-1806: Part of various small territories in the Holy Roman Empire (Ortenau region)
- 1806: Becomes part of the enlarged Grand Duchy of Baden; Durbach is in Amt Offenburg
- 1871: Joins German Empire; standard FamilySearch place name "Durbach, Offenburg, Baden" applies through 1871
- 1945–1952: Part of the French-zone "State of Baden"; 1952 merger creates Baden-Württemberg
- **Research implication:** FamilySearch Catalog organizes all German records by 1871 Meyer's Gazetteer place names — search as "Durbach, Amt Offenburg, Baden" in the catalog ([Germany Research Tips](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies))

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Civil registration in Baden began **1 January 1876** at the Standesamt level ([Baden, German Empire Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Baden,_German_Empire_Civil_Registration))
- **Applicability:** Civil registration postdates the 1800–1835 target window entirely. No civil birth, marriage, or death certificates exist for Creszentia Haas's christening period
- **Pre-registration source:** Catholic parish registers are the sole record source for this period

### Church records
- **Denomination:** Roman Catholic, Archdiocese of Freiburg im Breisgau
- **Durbach parish name:** Katholische Kirche Durbach (A. Offenburg)
- **FamilySearch Catalog entry:** [Kirchenbuch: 1655–1900](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/283948) — covers baptisms (Taufen), marriages, deaths
- **Language:** German (Kurrent script); earlier entries may use Latin formulae
- **FamilySearch volumes for Durbach** (all browse-only, 0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable):

| Volume ID | Record type | Date range |
|---|---|---|
| 007991190_002_M9XN-GWH | Taufen (baptisms) + Marriages | 1774–1804; 1780–1824 |
| 008104152_001_M9FS-5MH | Taufen (baptisms) | 1805–1838 |
| 008207894_001_M9FZ-FMN | Religious marriage records | 1824–1873 |
| 008207895_002_M9FZ-X2P | Religious death records | 1815–1852 |

- **Indexed collection:** [Germany, Baden, Archdiocese of Freiburg im Breisgau, Catholic Church Records, 1463–1931](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2790181) (FS collection 2790181) — 1,709,697 images, 623,353 indexed records. Durbach is included. Indexed + images at the collection level, though the specific Durbach volumes report 0% name-indexed (see Research Tips)
- **Church Book Duplicates:** [Germany, Baden, Church Book Duplicates, 1804–1877](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1395660) (FS collection 1395660) — **Durbach is NOT listed among the parishes covered** by this collection; do not rely on it for Durbach

### Census records
- No German national census was taken in the 1800–1835 period. Baden had no state census in this window that survives in accessible digitized form
- Parish-level ecclesiastical registers (Familienbücher/family registers) sometimes supplement baptismal records

### Probate and court records
- Court records for Amt Offenburg may name family members in property matters; held at Staatsarchiv Freiburg
- Not a primary source for birth/christening data but can confirm family relationships

### Land records
- Held at Generallandesarchiv Karlsruhe (Northern Baden) and Staatsarchiv Freiburg (Southern Baden — Offenburg is Southern Baden)
- Not digitized online for the 1800–1835 period

### Military records
- Napoleonic-era conscription records may exist for Baden males; held at Generallandesarchiv Karlsruhe

## Research tips
1. **Search the indexed collection first.** Run a name search in collection 2790181 ([Baden Catholic Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2790181)) for "Creszentia Haas" (or "Creszen\*"). The collection is indexed and images are linked; this is the fastest path ([Baden Online Genealogy Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Baden_Online_Genealogy_Records))
2. **Browse the Durbach Taufen volumes directly if the index misses her.** The 1805–1838 Taufen volume (008104152_001_M9FS-5MH) and the 1774–1804 volume (007991190_002_M9XN-GWH) cover all plausible birth years. Access via FamilySearch catalog #283948. Records are in Kurrent German script
3. **Also browse the Landesarchiv Freiburg portal.** Go to [Staatsarchiv Freiburg duplicate registers](https://www2.landesarchiv-bw.de/ofs21/olf/struktur.php?bestand=10028), click Amtsgerichtsbezirk Offenburg, find Durbach, select the religion (Katholische) and time period. This is an independent digital copy that may be cleaner or have different image quality from the FamilySearch copy ([Baden, German Empire Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Baden,_German_Empire_Church_Records))
4. **Do NOT search the Church Book Duplicates collection (1395660) for Durbach** — it does not cover Durbach parish ([Baden, German Empire Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Baden,_German_Empire_Church_Records))
5. **Civil registration does not apply.** Baden civil registration began 1 January 1876, after Creszentia's birth period entirely ([Baden, German Empire Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Baden,_German_Empire_Civil_Registration))
6. **Search neighboring parishes if not found in Durbach.** The Amt Offenburg includes Appenweier (Evangelische Kirche, nearby), Gengenbach, and Lahr-area parishes. The Dundenheim Catholic parish (A. Lahr) lies nearby and has a Kirchenbuch 1793–1900. If Creszentia was born in a neighboring village, her christening will be in that village's register, not Durbach's ([Germany Research Tips](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Research_Tips_and_Strategies))
7. **Use the marriage record as a cross-reference.** The 1855 christening record of Genofeva Haas should name the parents (Creszentia and her husband) and often gives the father's origin parish; the parents' marriage record (in the Durbach Heiraten registers) may state both spouses' birthplaces and ages, directly yielding Creszentia's birth year and home parish
8. **Kurrent handwriting.** All records are in old German script (Kurrent). Use the [German Genealogical Word List](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/German_Genealogical_Word_List) and the [Old German Script tutorials](https://www.familysearch.org/help/helpcenter/lessons/old-german-script-part-1)
9. **Creszentia is a Latin-derived saint's name** (St. Crescentia, feast day 15 June). In Catholic Baden, the feast-day naming convention was common; dates in old church records may reference feast days rather than calendar dates — use the [Moveable and Fixed Feast Day Calendars](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Moveable_and_Fixed_Feast_Day_Calendars_for_Germany) as a conversion aid
10. **Check for an Ortsfamilienbuch for Durbach.** A compiled family book for Durbach would reconstruct all families from the parish registers in one searchable database. Check [Baden OFB list](http://www.badische-ortsfamilienbuecher.de/buecher.php?sprache=DE&N=2#pathway) and [online-ofb.de](https://www.online-ofb.de/) — if one exists it will dramatically speed up the search
